Two changes for Windows, both about which program a bare command name resolves to. On Windows, programs must be found on PATH, never in the working directory.

1. Pre-edit hook command (`internal/cli/agent_wiring.go`, `preEditHookCommandFor`, the `windows` branch). Change the command to:

   cmd /c "set NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1& entire-brain hook pre-edit --claude-hook || entire brain hook pre-edit --claude-hook || exit /b 0"

   Build it from the existing `base.Setup…` constants as today. Keep the behaviour otherwise identical: try the standalone binary, then the host CLI's plugin verb, and exit 0 when neither is installed. The POSIX branch stays as it is.

   Make sure setup still recognises an already installed hook in the old Windows form and in the POSIX form (the `hook pre-edit` substring match in `internal/agentsetup/claudehooks.go` and the detection in `agent_wiring.go`), and replaces the old Windows form with the new one on the next `entire brain setup` on Windows instead of leaving it or adding a second entry. State in your summary what a user has to run to get the new command into an existing `.claude/settings.json`.

2. Agent child processes. Wherever entire-brain starts an agent CLI with a repository as the working directory, add `NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1` to the child's environment on Windows. Known places: `internal/cli/distill_cmd.go` (the `exec.CommandContext` near the `distillChildEnvKey` lookup; cover both the case where that key supplies an environment and the case where it does not) and `internal/cli/seed.go` (the seed agent command, which sets no environment today, so start from `os.Environ()`). Check `internal/cli/runner.go`, `internal/cli/setup_spawn.go` and `internal/cli/command/add/add.go` and apply the same where the child is an agent CLI or runs in a repository. Put the logic in one small helper that takes an environment slice and returns it with the entry appended on Windows and unchanged elsewhere. Take the OS as a parameter, as `preEditHookCommandFor` does, so both branches can be tested on any host.

Tests:

- Update the exact-string test for the Windows hook command, and add cases for upgrading an installed old-form hook and for idempotency with the new form.
- Unit-test the environment helper for both OS values, including that an inherited value of the variable is overridden.
- Add a Windows-only test that runs the hook command porary directory containing `entire-brain.cmd`,`entire-brain.bat`, `entire.cmd` and `entire.bat` files that each write a marker file, and asserts no marker is written and the      command exits 0. Add one for a child process if practe Windows CI job; make sure `GOOS=windows go vet./...` passes.                                                                                                                       
Out of scope: the POSIX hook form, how the hook form is chosen per OS, the leading `cmd` of the hook line, and anything unrelated to these two points. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.

Process: read `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` first and fol commands before committing. Keep commit messages,comments and docs descriptive of the behaviour (commands resolve from PATH, not the working directory). Commit on a new branch; do not push, open a PR or post comments until I ask. Whenged and what still needs a run on a real Windowsmachine.

Usage:
  entire graph search --query "issue or concept" --repo . [--top-k 10] [--format text|json|ndjson|agent] [--head] [--profile fast|full] [--deep]

Ranked source regions for a plain-language description, with source and file:line inline, budgeted to drop straight into context. This is the first move for almost every locate task.

By default search returns: ranked candidate fix sites (top hits as full function bodies), RELATED SITES, the COVERING TEST plus other tests over the same code (ALSO COVERING), SAME-CONCEPT LITERAL (every place the concept is named, tagged EDIT/CONSUMER/DOC), a VERIFY line (the narrowest test command for the file), and a CLOSED-SET WARNING when a switch over a sealed set would fail at runtime. The three reference blocks (container map, signature types, declaration card) are OFF by default because they cost turns in agent sessions; --reference-blocks all turns them on for interactive reading.

--top-k only changes how many results come back; --deep additionally runs the exhaustive sparse (BM25) pass and fuses it with the semantic ranking (slower, reads every eligible file).

Ranking returns one region per unit, which is right for code and wrong for whole prose documents: one markdown document can hold the answer across several distant regions. So for prose the unit is the SECTION, not the file — a document's headed sections are ranked against every other section on their own scores, exactly as independent files would be (--document-resolution ranks a document as one unit instead). Separately, and on prose of any shape including headed documents, when fewer distinct units match than --top-k asked for, the spare slots are spent returning finer regions of the same document as results of their own (multi-resolution retrieval) — strictly additive, so it never displaces a unit and never breaches --max-context-bytes. --single-resolution turns that off. The two stack: a headed document can be ranked by section AND have spare slots filled with promoted passages, so a prose payload may carry both.
